clue.text: Knights are members of the board

definitions.text: Knights are members of the board

parts.words: Knights are members of the board
parts.note: reads like knighted directors on a company board, but the board is a chequered one and knights are pieces that sit on it

explanation.surface: Titled businessmen sit as directors of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights, like bishops and rooks, are pieces used on the chequered board in the game of kings and queens.

clue.text: Plant a malcontent in the house of lords

indicators.note: the clue words a malcontent are placed inside the abbreviation for the upper chamber

parts.note: HL is the standard abbreviation for the House of Lords, the UK's upper chamber of Parliament
a malcontent is a rebel, someone discontented with authority

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is planted among the peers of the upper chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb (place a spy) but is the definition. The House of Lords is the unelected upper chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The harebell is a wild flower with blue bell-shaped blooms, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Gymnastic Samuel strums then leaps about

indicators.note: the letters perform gymnastic tumbles, so the names and verb that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Samuel plays his guitar and then bounds around the room like an acrobat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gymnastic' rearranges SAMUEL STRUMS. The answer is a variant spelling of SOMERSAULTS, used by this setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A somersault is a head-over-heels leap, so these acrobatic flips are leaps about, turning round in the air.

clue.text: I object to Alan, for instance, finding the maize

parts.note: the objective case of I is me
Al is the short form of the name Alan
i.e. (that is) here stands in for an example phrase

explanation.surface: Someone feels offended when Alan comes across the maize field.
explanation.walkthrough: MEALIE is South African English for maize or a maize cob. The setter uses IE loosely for 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mealie is the South African word for Indian corn, the cereal crop also called corn.

clue.text: Not off-side but close

definitions.meaning: the ... side of a horse or vehicle is the left, the opposite of the off side
close means nearby, not far away

explanation.definitionFit: Near side is the opposite of off side in horse and road usage, and near means at a short distance.

clue.text: Graze caused by adult underwear I put on

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
bras are items of women's underwear
on means worn, as clothes put on

explanation.surface: A grown-up gets a skin graze from the underwear they put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A graze is a scrape that rubs off skin, the sort of injury caused by friction.

clue.text: A keen gardener locates this tree

indicators.note: the tree is found sitting inside the opening words of the clue, located within them

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic gardener spots a particular tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The akee (ackee) is a tropical tree whose fruit is eaten in Jamaica.

clue.text: Issues about sedition

indicators.note: about signals the letters of sedition are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Published matters concern incitement against the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Editions are the separate printings of a newspaper or book, each one an issue.

clue.text: As ark in fix, firmly boarded the ship

indicators.note: the word ark is placed in the middle of the word for fixing firmly

parts.note: to embed something is to fix it firmly in place

explanation.surface: Animals in a tight spot go up the gangplank as if onto Noah's ark.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go on board a vessel at the start of a voyage.

clue.text: A follower on the edge of the verge

parts.note: B follows A in the alphabet
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A disciple stands at the very edge of a grassy roadside strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verge' suggests a roadside strip but here means the edge itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The brim of a cup is its uppermost border, just as a verge is a margin or border.

clue.text: Lament matter concerning bullying

indicators.note: concerning in the sense of troubling or disturbing, so the letters of the two words are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone bemoans an issue relating to intimidation in the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning' looks like 'about', but in its troubling sense it shuffles LAMENT MATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullying is cruel, harmful treatment of someone, a form of abuse.

clue.text: Computer component with extremely small perimeter

parts.note: micro means very tiny
a circuit is the boundary line going round an area

explanation.surface: A tiny part inside a computer has a very short outer edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A microcircuit is a tiny integrated electronic circuit, a basic building block of computers.

clue.text: It's unique not to look too closely

parts.note: to peer is to look searchingly and closely
less can mean without or minus, a negative

explanation.surface: Someone says it is singular not to scrutinise things too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: look closely (PEER) less.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means without equal, having no match, so one of a kind.

clue.text: Finishes up at the highest place in the ship

indicators.note: the highest place is put in the abbreviation for a steamship

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
the top is the uppermost position

explanation.surface: A sailor ends up at the masthead of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop is to come to an end, halt or cease, as the verb 'finishes' does.

clue.text: In Colorado a virtuoso originates an intaglio

annotationWithheld.why: In Colorado a virtuoso originates an intaglio (6): INCAVO reads as IN + initials of Colorado, a, virtuoso, originates, so 'originates' must both signal first letters and supply the O
annotationWithheld.clue: In Colorado a virtuoso originates an intaglio

clue.text: The two states of seaweed

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Alabama
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Two conditions in which marine weed can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' suggests conditions, but it means two American states, Alabama and Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: An alga is a simple water plant; seaweeds are large marine examples.

clue.text: Means to affirm the time

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert firmly
ages are eras or periods of time

explanation.surface: Methods for stating the hour with confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Means in the statistical sense are averages, typical central values of a set.

clue.text: Toast Gordon!

definitions.meaning: to toast bread is to ... it under heat
Gordon ... was UK Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010

explanation.definitionFit: Toasting bread makes it brown, and Gordon Brown was a British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Wrap of eiderdown

parts.note: describes a quilt stuffed with duck feathers that is wrapped over a sleeper at night

explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt laid over a bed, so it serves as a covering for sleepers.

clue.text: Eyes dour abuse regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words dour abuse

explanation.surface: Someone stares out after repeated harsh mistreatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbs is a poetic word for eyeballs, the round organs of sight.

clue.text: Poised with a weapon in poor neighbourhood

indicators.note: a and the weapon are placed in the word for a poor area

parts.note: a bad neighbourhood is a rough, poor part of town
a lance is a long spear carried by mounted knights

explanation.surface: Someone stands steady holding a spear in a rough part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Poised means held steady in equilibrium, not tipping either way.

clue.text: Former spouse I directed to be outlawed

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
led means guided or directed

explanation.surface: A former partner I steered was banned from the land.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exiled is to be banished from one's country, like an outlaw driven out.

clue.text: Birds — spotted fliers

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see, as spotted means noticed
fliers (flyers) are leaflets or posters, also called bills

explanation.surface: Someone noticed birds in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fliers' looks like birds again but means printed handbills.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbills are ducks such as mergansers with serrated beaks, a group of waterfowl.

clue.text: Power unit the French use materially on the roof

parts.note: the watt is the SI unit of power
le is the masculine form of the in French

explanation.surface: Electrical power and French grammar are applied to roofing materials.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: wattle, woven twigs, is a material used for walls, fences and roofs.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle is interwoven rods and branches, a traditional building material for roofs and walls.

clue.text: A strict Cairo practice belonging to the privileged

indicators.note: practice suggests drilling or working over, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rigorous custom in Cairo is reserved for the elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocratic describes the nobility, the high-born upper class enjoying special privilege.

clue.text: Idaho and new York lock horns to hold a motor race

indicators.note: the two state abbreviations clash and one grips the letter for new inside it

parts.note: ID is the postal abbreviation for Idaho
Y is the first letter used here for York

explanation.surface: Two US places clash over hosting a car race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indy, short for the Indianapolis 500, is an American motor race. ID and NY interlock in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indianapolis 500 is a famous American car race, often called the Indy.

clue.text: Frozen dew I'm surrounded by again

indicators.note: the letters of I'm are surrounded by the word for again

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone surrounded by frost once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is hoar frost, the ice crystals that form when dew or mist freezes.

clue.text: A French business in Scotland is remarkable

parts.note: un is the French for a
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A French firm in Scotland is extraordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Scotland' says the answer is a Scots word: unco means unusual or remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unco is Scots for strange or extraordinary, so something unusual and striking.

clue.text: Fragment of nothing but a skin layer of cells

parts.note: an end is a remnant or scrap, as in odds and ends
O looks like zero, nothing
derm means skin, as in dermatology

explanation.surface: A scrap of nothing but a thin coat of tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: The endoderm is the innermost germ layer of an embryo, a sheet of tissue.

clue.text: Occasion to fish before nightfall

parts.note: an event is an occasion
the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe

explanation.surface: A chance to go fishing before dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the time when darkness falls.
